title: Continuous cochains preserve short exact sequences of discrete modules
statement: Let $G$ be a profinite group, $A$ a finite ring, and $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$ a short exact sequence in the abelian category of left $A$-modules with continuous $A$-linear $G$-action [lem-exc-discrete-modules-abelian]. Give these modules the discrete topology. For every $n\geq0$, the sequence $0\to\operatorname{Cont}(G^n,M')\to\operatorname{Cont}(G^n,M)\to\operatorname{Cont}(G^n,M'')\to0$ is exact. The maps commute with the inhomogeneous group-cochain differentials, namely $d^0m(g)=gm-m$ and, for $n\geq1$, $d^nf(g_1,\ldots,g_{n+1})=g_1f(g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1})+\sum_{j=1}^n(-1)^jf(g_1,\ldots,g_jg_{j+1},\ldots,g_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}f(g_1,\ldots,g_n)$; hence they form a short exact sequence of cochain complexes of $A$-modules.

source.place: Tag 0DVG, label section-continuous-group-cohomology, paragraph beginning 'However, a short exact sequence of discrete G-modules'

proof.text: Write $i:M'\to M$ and $p:M\to M''$. Exactness in [lem-exc-discrete-modules-abelian] is exactness of the underlying $A$-modules. For each $n$, postcomposition with $i$ is injective. If $p\circ f=0$ for a continuous $f:G^n\to M$, then every $f(x)$ lies in $i(M')$; the unique pointwise preimage $f':G^n\to M'$ is continuous because $M'$ and $M$ are discrete and the inverse image of each singleton under $f'$ is an inverse image under $f$ of a singleton in $M$. Thus the image of postcomposition with $i$ is the kernel of postcomposition with $p$. Choose a set-theoretic section $s:M''\to M$ of the surjection $p$. Both modules are discrete, so $s$ is continuous; for any continuous $h:G^n\to M''$, the map $s\circ h$ is a continuous lift. Hence postcomposition with $p$ is surjective. For $n=0$, $G^0$ is a singleton and this is the original exact sequence.

source.place: Tag 0DVG, label section-continuous-group-cohomology, paragraph beginning 'However, a short exact sequence of discrete G-modules'; the pointwise lifting argument is supplied here

proof.text: The displayed formula defines a continuous $A$-linear differential: each projection, adjacent multiplication map $G^{n+1}\to G^n$, and the action map $G\times M\to M$ is continuous, and finite sums are continuous into the discrete module. The identity $d^{n+1}d^n=0$ follows by expanding the two alternating sums: terms joining disjoint adjacent pairs occur twice with opposite signs, as do the action term paired with joining the first pair and the final omission term paired with joining the last pair; the remaining double-action terms cancel by $(g_1g_2)m=g_1(g_2m)$. In degree zero, the two terms from $d^1(d^0m)$ cancel directly. Thus these are cochain complexes.

source.place: Tag 0DVG, label section-continuous-group-cohomology, displayed inhomogeneous differential; the cancellation check is supplied here

proof.text: For either equivariant $A$-linear map $u=i,p$, applying $u$ to every term in the formula for $d^nf$ gives the corresponding term of $d^n(u\circ f)$: $u(gm)=g u(m)$ handles the first term, and additivity handles the alternating sum and last term. The degree-zero formula has the same property. Therefore the degreewise maps of Step 1 are morphisms of the complexes of Step 2 and their composite is zero. Extend these nonnegative complexes by zero in negative degrees. Their degreewise sequences are short exact in every integer degree, so the criterion [lem-weil-pbc-cochain-complexes-degreewise-exact] makes the resulting sequence short exact as complexes; restricting back to nonnegative degrees gives the asserted cochain-complex sequence.
